title: incident-bot: oncall runbook autodiagnostics priority ranking and heuristics
author: Lena Park
release_notes: Improves incident-bot runbook suggestion ranking by adding a priority scoring function that uses SLO correlation, past runbook success, and on-call ownership; adds feature flag and telemetry; updates docs and dashboards.
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers rely on incident-bot to surface the most relevant runbooks and quick actions when SLOs or alerts fire. Previously runbook suggestions were primarily keyword/label-based and surfaced multiple low-value results, increasing on-call cognitive load and time-to-action. This PR introduces a priority ranking layer for runbook autodiagnostics that factors SLO correlation, historical success rate, recency, and current on-call ownership.

What this PR does: Adds a prioritizer component that scores candidate runbooks and autodiagnostic suggestions. Score factors: SLO correlation (weight 0.4), historical success (0.3), runbook recency/last-updated (0.15), on-call owner affinity (0.1), and user-feedback boost (0.05). The prioritizer is pluggable and feature-flagged. Key changes include: updated prioritizer implementation in pkg/autodiag/prioritizer.go, a lightweight python scoring util for batch analytics in slo-toolkit/heuristics/ranking.py, API additions to incident-bot to return ranked suggestions (cmd/incident-bot/handlers/runbooks.go), dashboard metrics and alerts (observability/dashboards/runbook-priority.jsonnet), and docs/runbook guidance updates.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag incident_bot.autodiag_priority (default off). Start with 10% sampled traffic for internal teams, monitor prediction quality (precision@3), time-to-ack, and oncall feedback. Gradual rollout to 100% after 2 weeks of positive signal. Fallback policy: if scoring service times out or returns error, we fall back to baseline keyword ranking.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for prioritizer scoring logic and edge cases (scores for missing metadata, zero-history runbooks). Integration tests added to simulate SLO-linked alerts and ensure suggestions are consistently ranked and returned within the latency SLO (95th < 120ms for suggestion endpoint). Canary experiment harness added to perf-canary for end-to-end validation.

Operational notes: Added telemetry counters: runbook.rank.count, runbook.rank.latency_ms, runbook.rank.failure, and histogram runbook.score.distribution. Dashboard and alert playbook provided. Migration: a small schema change to the runbook metadata store to add last_success_count and last_attempt_ts (backfilled via a migration job included). Migration is non-blocking and default values are safe.

Related: Linear ENG-1942 for prioritizer epic; SRE-312 for rollout and monitoring.

Checklist:
- [x] Prioritizer algorithm and tests
- [x] API changes and backwards-compatible response shape (rank score added to suggestion items)
- [x] Feature flag and rollout config
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard
- [x] Migration script and backfill job
- [x] Docs updated

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about weights; we expect to iterate on the model and surface instrumentation to tune for different services. Performance impact measured during local perf-canary runs is <5% additional CPU on the suggestion path and latency budget remains within target when running in the Dedicated dev pool.
